title: convoy: no test pins ClientSource's raw dependency read against a real Dolt store (the fake-vs-Dolt parity test went with fakeRigStore)
notes: Found by lapis in gt-7iwy0.3.1: TestIntegrationFakeStoreMatchesDolt compared the beadsdk test fake (fakeRigStore) against a real Dolt store through testutil.OpenTestStore; it went with fakeRigStore. The unit tests now pin ClientSource's raw reads against a scripted bd-sql answer (fake_source_test.go answerRawDeps), which follows beadsql.RawDeps' exact statement text, but nothing exercises the read against real Dolt. internal/convoy's integration tier now has only its TestMain.

title: Daemon-raised escalations record the daemon as escalated_by, not 'overseer'
description:
## Goal
hq-wisp-btoyzk (checkpoint_dog revert guard, raised by the daemon) showed 'Escalated by: overseer', misattributing an automated alert to the operator.
## Constraints
internal/daemon escalation path and internal/notify or the escalate sender detection it uses.
## Out of scope
Escalation routing and severity.
## Gate
make lint, make gate
## Size
one worker, one landing
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An escalation raised through Daemon.escalateAlertSeverity (internal/daemon/jsonl_git_backup.go:944) shows Escalated by: daemon (or daemon/<source>), never the town overseer identity; test with a fake notifier
- [ ] Escalations raised by agents still record the agent address; test
- [ ] make lint && make gate pass

title: Remaining rig.LoadRigConfig callers in daemon, schedulerrun and doctor still swallow a parse error
description:
gt-w8dw5 routed the call sites it named through rig.LoadRigConfigIfPresent. The same 'if err == nil' fallback remains at:
- internal/daemon/daemon.go:2095 (beads prefix)
- internal/daemon/landing_worker.go:745 (default_branch)
- internal/daemon/checkpoint_dog.go:293 (default_branch)
- internal/rig/manager.go RegisterRig (~1707, reuses an existing config.json)
- internal/schedulerrun/validate.go:146 (beads prefix)
- internal/doctor/rig_beads_check.go:155 (git URL; doctor has a dedicated unreadable-config check, so confirm double-reporting is acceptable before changing it)
With strict decoding (gt-y3pgh.2.5) a typo'd key at any of these degrades silently, exactly where fail-closed wants it loud.
